issues.title: [P1][RFC] Define cross-session continuation, transfer, and evidence composition protocols
issues.body:
## Problem

"Move a player from A to B" can mean continuing the same game, transferring an item, or combining evidence from two matches into a season result. These operations need different correctness guarantees. Define the protocols before expanding the interfaces.

Audit baseline: Myelin 0.31.0, commit `c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2`. Successors and source-committed handoffs already exist. Handoff lookup, source-block access, and consumption markers currently depend on one SessionStore. This RFC extends their supported scope.

## Proposed model

| Operation | Required invariant | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Successor / continuation | Seal the source and bind its unique successor to the exact final state and new configuration | Authority rotation, season continuation, rule upgrades |
| Handoff / transfer | Specify source-side disposition and the recipient; atomically commit consumption with target state | Inventory migration, match rewards |
| Stitching / composition | Verify each history and its causal relationships without claiming merged writes or consensus | Cross-game achievements, tournament evidence, history views |
| Remote collaboration | Sessions commit independently and express dependencies through asynchronous messages | Multi-room tournaments, cross-service tasks |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["Cross-session requirement"] --> Q{"What changes?"}
  Q -->|"Continue an entire history"| S["Seal source and create one successor"]
  Q -->|"Transfer scarce state or rights"| H["Source lock and target consumption"]
  Q -->|"Combine results and histories"| C["Verify receipts and dependency graph"]
  H --> D{"Shared authoritative store?"}
  D -->|"Yes"| L["Local atomic consumption"]
  D -->|"No"| P["Independent proofs and terminal-state coordination"]
```

## Design deliverables

- Define versioned identity domains for deployment/network, session genesis, application profile, authority/consensus descriptor, object/claim, command, and handoff.
- Define an immutable envelope binding source genesis and exact block hash/height/root, target session or constrained policy, participants, payload schema, authorization, expiry, evidence policy, and capability type.
- Distinguish copyable evidence, nonexclusive cosmetic snapshots, and exclusively consumable rights. Copying a result receipt must not imply copying a tradable item.
- Start v1 with a shared store and explicit targets. Specify policy-target competition, writers across processes, and remote terminal states separately. Disable remote multi-target scarce claims by default.
- Specify time semantics and boundaries. Current expiry uses the target block timestamp; this does not establish a trusted wall-clock refund deadline.
- State safety and liveness requirements: unique consumption, conservation, configuration binding, and recovery. A partition may leave work pending; retries must not duplicate rights.
- Keep cross-game schema conversion in explicit adapters. Do not automatically concatenate raw state or signatures from different rule sets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publish the ADR, proposed types, state machines, error table, and threat/failure assumptions.
- [ ] Include examples for one store, separate stores, different authorities, and outstanding messages after source sealing.
- [ ] Identify who supplies shared-store atomicity, cross-store coordination, application authorization, and L1 enforcement.
- [ ] Publish golden vectors usable without a private platform database.
- [ ] Build on implemented capabilities without assigning consensus responsibilities to a Registry or relay.

Related: [Myelin#10](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/10), [Myelin#11](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/11), [Myelin#16](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/16), [Myelin#17](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/17), [Myelin#14](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/14). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

## Source evidence

[continuity.rs](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/continuity.rs), [prepare_block](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L1057), [RocksDB consumption transaction](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-store-rocksdb/src/lib.rs).

issues.title: [P1] Separate handoff expiry, evidence-gate, and competing-consumer regression tests
issues.body:
## Current behavior and impact

`handoff_is_source_committed_target_bound_expiring_and_single_use` creates ordinary, evidence-gated, and expired handoffs in that order, but names index 1 `expired_id` and index 2 `gated_id`. Its negative assertions check only `is_err()`.

An isolated probe confirmed that both production checks work: an unexpired request without evidence reports "required handoff evidence is absent"; an expired request reports "handoff target policy mismatch or handoff expired". This task improves test clarity and coverage. It does not establish a gate bypass.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  F["Three explicitly named fixtures"] --> V["Ordinary and unexpired"]
  F --> E["Unexpired with insufficient evidence"]
  F --> X["Sufficient evidence but expired"]
  V --> A["Consumption succeeds"]
  E --> R1["Evidence rejection"]
  X --> R2["Expiry rejection"]
```

## Scope

- Return IDs from named fixtures instead of positional indices.
- Make each negative case violate exactly one precondition. Assert the precise error category; introduce structured continuity errors if necessary.
- Add successful consumption after sufficient evidence, wrong pipeline/stage cases, the expiry equality boundary, and condition changes between prepare and commit.
- Prepare consumption in two policy-matching targets concurrently. Only one shared-store commit may succeed.
- Cover pre-consumption failure, process exit after consumption, restart queries, duplicate consumption, and marker tampering. Unknown commit outcomes enter reconciliation.
- Check atomicity across consumption, command receipts, target state, and outbox rather than inspecting only the marker.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Removing or weakening a gate makes its dedicated negative test fail.
- [ ] A positive evidence-gated case succeeds; do not test only permanent rejection.
- [ ] Competing consumers and restart recovery produce at most one effect.
- [ ] Preserve the existing 756-test workspace record and report new coverage separately.

Complete this before extending [Myelin#11](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/11) and [Myelin#16](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/16). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[Existing test](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-store-rocksdb/tests/store.rs#L656), [target validation](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L1101).

issues.title: [P1] Add aggregate budgets for handoffs, outbox effects, snapshots, and host execution
issues.body:
## A concrete example

`max_block_bytes` counts CellTx bytes, while ApplicationResourceEnvelope limits frame payloads. Neither is an aggregate bound on the complete commit record.

The audit probe prepared and committed a block with a 1,000,001-byte handoff payload under `max_block_bytes = 1,000,000` and zero CellTx bytes. Individual handoffs and outbox messages have fixed limits, but their counts and aggregate sizes need equally explicit budgets. This is a resource-model gap, not a reproduced public-network attack.

A host Rust replayer returning `cycles = 0` also does not mean it consumes no CPU, memory, or execution time.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  I["Request and input"] --> P["Pre-execution budgets"]
  P --> E["Isolated host or VM execution"]
  E --> O["Aggregate output and effect budgets"]
  O --> C["Atomic commit"]
  P --> R["Reject over-budget work"]
  O --> R
```

## Proposed implementation

- Distinguish CellTx bytes, frame input, issued/consumed handoff counts and bytes, authorization bytes, commitment count, outbox count/bytes, and snapshot/record bytes.
- Commit protocol-validity limits in genesis/profile. Configure operational queue, disk, and timeout limits separately from consensus rules.
- Use checked arithmetic. Validate predictable sizes before execution/allocation and validate outputs before durable writes.
- Bound decoded lengths and nested structures; rejection must not first allocate arbitrary memory.
- Define terminable process/worker isolation and memory limits for host execution. An asynchronous timeout cannot terminate a synchronous infinite loop.
- Apply equivalent budgets and clear errors to replay, recovery, and offline bundle import.
- Version commitment formats and document compatibility rather than silently reinterpreting old profiles.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cover zero CellTx, many small handoffs, large outboxes, multiple authorizations, and abnormal snapshots at their boundaries.
- [ ] Rejection leaves the head, receipts, handoff markers, and outbox unchanged.
- [ ] Measure host wall time/RSS separately from VM cycles.
- [ ] Document the current meaning of `max_block_bytes` and the new aggregate limits.

Design dependency: [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7). Used by [Myelin#19](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/19) and [Myelin#20](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/20). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[Resource structures](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/application.rs#L36), [CellTx byte calculation](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L1080), [per-handoff limits](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/continuity.rs), [OutboxMessage](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L217).

issues.title: [P1] Validate source handoff and successor declarations through replayable application authorization
issues.body:
## Why this is needed

Including a payload in a signed block proves that an authority committed to that statement. It does not automatically prove an item was debited from the source inventory or its owner authorized migration.

The caller supplies `BlockRequest.handoffs` and `successor`. `TransitionExecutor::execute_block` receives consumed handoffs but not issued intents or the successor request. Source handoffs are constructed after application execution. The primitive can represent trusted-host declarations, but does not by itself supply general asset-transfer semantics.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C["Original command and authorization"] --> V["Validate protocol intent"]
  V --> S["Application state change or lock"]
  S --> H["Derive handoff and successor declarations"]
  H --> F["Verify finality"]
  F --> A["Atomically commit state, declarations, and outbox"]
```

## Proposed deliverable

Choose and justify an interface: include intents in deterministic execution context, derive verifiable effects from ExecutionOutcome, or require a ProtocolEffectsVerifier. Source replay must reject unauthorized effects rather than merely append their hashes again.

- Bind authorization to source genesis, actor, exact object/version, target/policy, payload, expiry, and nonce. Platform login cannot serve as asset-migration authorization.
- Executors without an issuance/migration policy must reject these effects, or explicitly classify them as authority metadata that economic intake cannot promote into stronger claims.
- A scarce-transfer policy checks source locking/debiting; a copyable-receipt policy explicitly permits copying.
- Bind successor authorization to the full target configuration, including new program, consensus, authority, resource, and time rules.
- Apply equivalent rules during initial execution, replay, offline verification, and any future court path.
- Economic profiles must reject a handoff claiming a debit without the required source-state change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Changing recipient, amount, object/version, expiry, or new authority causes rejection.
- [ ] Missing source locks/debits, arbitrary nonempty authorization, and duplicate intents fail.
- [ ] A valid local transfer replays to the same effect commitment.
- [ ] Hosts can implement custom policies, with their trust model visible in exports.
- [ ] Documentation describes work toward transfer semantics, not an already implemented cross-game bridge.

Depends on [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7); supports [Myelin#11](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/11), [Myelin#14](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/14), and [Myelin#17](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/17). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[Execution interface and request](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L296), [source handoff derivation](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L1190), [replay](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/replay.rs).

issues.title: [P1] Implement a shared-store reference state machine for session transfer and cancellation
issues.body:
## Scenario

After match A finishes, credit inventory B with one reward, or move a character from room A to B. The system must establish the required source-side disposition and exactly one target effect.

RocksDB already commits handoff consumption markers atomically with target blocks, and policy-matching targets can compete in one store. Build an application state machine and recovery example on these foundations.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Available
  Available --> Locked: Source authorization and commit
  Locked --> Consumed: Atomic target consumption and credit
  Locked --> Cancelled: Authoritative cancellation permanently blocks consumption
  Cancelled --> Available: Source refund transaction
  Consumed --> [*]
```

## Scope

- Define a versioned TransferPayload binding object, owner, target, source-state version, amount/components, and intake schema. Games need not share one inventory format.
- Atomically commit source lock/debit with handoff issuance; atomically commit target marker, credit, receipt, and outbox.
- Do not treat StoredHandoff's current consumed markers as a complete lock/cancel lifecycle.
- Shared-store cancellation and consumption must compete over the same authoritative terminal-state key. A later idempotent transaction may refund the source; never refund before committing cancellation.
- Expiry invalidates intake but does not automatically restore source rights. Follow [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7) for time semantics; a backdated target timestamp must not bypass cancellation.
- Provide controlled examples for explicit and policy targets. All competing policy targets share one uniqueness domain.
- Keep conflicts pending for reconciliation. Do not issue a second handoff as a retry.
- Expose issued/locked/consumed/cancelled/reclaimed states and their exact blocks. Distinguish missing records from unknown commit outcomes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only one of two competing targets can consume a handoff.
- [ ] Cancellation and consumption have one terminal outcome; source refunds cannot coexist with target credit.
- [ ] Crashes around source commit, target commit, ACK, cancellation, and refund preserve conservation after restart.
- [ ] Outstanding rights remain available for reconciliation whether the source continues or seals.
- [ ] The example runs and replays independently, without claiming an atomic transaction across separate RocksDB stores.

Depends on [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7), [Myelin#10](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/10), [Myelin#8](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/8), and [Myelin#9](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/9). Remote extensions: [Myelin#16](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/16), [Myelin#17](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/17). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[StoredHandoff](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/continuity.rs#L239), [atomic consumption](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-store-rocksdb/src/lib.rs), [local handoff test](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-store-rocksdb/tests/store.rs#L656).

issues.title: [P1] Provide a durable command journal and unknown-commit recovery reference adapter
issues.body:
## Problem

Version 0.31 already supplies durable CommandReceipt, construction heads, and OutcomeUnknown handling. Applications still need a complete journal. The bundled producer FIFO is explicitly an in-memory helper; it cannot alone recover pending commands and original authorization after restart.

Example: an item purchase commits, but its HTTP response is lost. A retry should recover the original result without charging twice.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Queued
  Queued --> Reserved: Persist reservation and construction head
  Reserved --> Committed: Query or commit returns exact receipt
  Reserved --> Unknown: Commit outcome is uncertain
  Unknown --> Committed: Reconciliation finds durable receipt
  Unknown --> Queued: Prove absence and fence previous writer
  Committed --> Acknowledged: Business result is recoverable
```

## Implementation boundary

- Persist the original canonical command, authentication context/authorization digest, stable command ID, payload hash, target session/profile, reservation, and construction head.
- A journal and SessionStore may be separate databases. Use idempotent writes and recovery coordination rather than claiming cross-database atomicity.
- Document actions for `Committed / IdentityConflict / Missing`. Missing does not authorize replay while the writer's outcome is unknown.
- Rebuild stale CellTx from the original command while retaining the same economic-intent identity. Do not assign a new ID to every retry.
- Keep reservations when durable commit succeeds but ACK fails. Release only definitely uncommitted or explicitly rejected work.
- Distinguish user commands, per-frame input tapes, and system timeout events; do not require wallet signatures on every 60Hz input sample.
- Expose stale/rejected/pending/committed outcomes. Receipt inclusion alone does not establish business success.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recover from crashes around journal write, reserve, prepare, commit, ACK, and HTTP response.
- [ ] The same ID and payload recover the original result; changed payloads fail; signatures prevent replay into another session.
- [ ] Rebuilding source work preserves valid queue prefixes and retains unknown reservations.
- [ ] Provide single-player inventory and two-player turn-based examples for [UTXOPlay#4](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/4).
- [ ] Preserve existing tape-profile interpretation; use a new profile for new command policies.

Build on completed #1 and #2 without reopening them. Related: [Myelin#15](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/15), [Myelin#19](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/19). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[Safety contracts](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/docs/architecture/session-safety.md), [commands.rs](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/commands.rs), [producer](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-producer/src/lib.rs).

issues.title: [P1] Define portable session evidence bundles and reproducible replayer manifests
issues.body:
## User and integrator need

An independent verifier downloading an old season's replay must know which program, rules, and authority key to use, even if the original service is offline. A nonzero program_digest or "verified=true" field is insufficient.

ApplicationProfile already commits program/input/state/time/entropy/court/handoff digests. RangeReplayReceipt binds an exact range. The missing piece is a consistent contract for obtaining, running, and auditing the required artifacts and bundles.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  G["Trusted genesis and policy anchors"] --> V["Offline verifier"]
  B["Versioned bundle manifest"] --> V
  A["Content-addressed historical programs, rules, and data"] --> V
  H["Blocks, proofs, inputs, checkpoint, and dependencies"] --> V
  V --> R["Layered verification report and deterministic result"]
```

## Deliverables

- Record format version, Myelin/schema/toolchain, genesis commitment, profile, consensus configuration/key, artifact hashes, checkpoint, block/frame ranges, complete handoff/successor dependencies, and resource limits.
- Specify trust bootstrap. A public key supplied by the bundle establishes internal consistency; recognizing an official game or intended session also requires an external trusted genesis/profile allowlist.
- Locate native/WASM replayers by immutable artifact digests and complete build inputs. Hashing selected source files alone does not prove reproducible binaries or complete dependency coverage.
- Report host replay, CellTx/CKB-VM verification, committee finality, DA, CKB inclusion, and court adjudication separately. New capability fields must not promote old evidence.
- Validate integrity, size, and dependency graphs on import. Unknown native programs require process/container isolation, not direct loading into the verifier process.
- Provide verify/export CLI commands, machine-readable errors, stable golden vectors, and offline verification for fully archived bundles.
- Include actor/seat admission and required timeout/entropy events while excluding unnecessary PII, login credentials, and private information.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Historical bundles produce the same root/result with their original verifier; new programs cannot silently reinterpret them.
- [ ] Tampering with code, rules, authority, network, input, dependency source blocks, or snapshots is detected.
- [ ] Missing artifacts, unknown trust anchors, and missing dependencies have distinct, understandable failures.
- [ ] Cross-session composition shows each profile, authority, and causal edge without claiming a combined security domain.
- [ ] Replay succeeds offline on a clean machine, with reports usable by [UTXOPlay#3](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/3).

Depends on [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7) and [Myelin#9](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/9); related: [Myelin#18](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/18), [Myelin#16](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/16), [Myelin#14](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/14). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[ApplicationProfile](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/application.rs#L76), [RangeReplayReceipt](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/replay.rs), [claim ladder](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/docs/security/claim-ladder.md).

issues.title: [P1] Add successor compatibility rules, migration evidence, and command inheritance semantics
issues.body:
## Existing capability and remaining gap

Successors already seal the source and create one target in the source-block transaction. They bind exact post-state, cursor, logical time, and timestamp, and require the same state_codec_hash. Preserve that foundation.

A matching codec only specifies how bytes are decoded. It does not prove how new rules interpret them. Program changes, authority rotation, season resets, and state-schema changes need separate rules.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S["Source finalized head"] --> K{"Migration category"}
  K -->|"Same state interpretation"| C["Continue state and bind new configuration"]
  K -->|"New rules with same codec"| P["Explicit compatibility policy and authorization"]
  K -->|"Codec or state conversion"| M["Separate migration program and input/output evidence"]
  C --> F["Seal source and create one successor"]
  P --> F
  M --> F
```

## Scope

- Publish a support matrix for same-program continuation, authority/committee rotation, rule upgrades, schema migration, and season resets. Implement a small supported subset first; reject unsupported paths explicitly.
- Validate the complete target configuration through [Myelin#10](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/10). Retain old genesis, finality verifiers, artifacts, and reverse lineage.
- Require compatibility declarations and vectors when a new program uses the same codec. Codec equality must not bypass program-change review.
- Use a separately versioned migration artifact/receipt for incompatible state conversion, binding old/new profiles, old/new roots, and migration inputs. Do not simply relax root equality and accept arbitrary new roots.
- Successors currently have separate command namespaces. Old signatures must bind the source session; pending commands need fresh authorization or explicit transfer.
- Define ownership of outstanding handoffs, pending outbox work, reward nullifiers, and external obligations so sealing neither loses work nor duplicates rewards.
- Resetting seasonal scores differs from continuing complete state. Do not represent an empty state as the predecessor's identical-root successor.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New authorities can finalize only the new session; old histories still use their old verifier.
- [ ] Reject wrong predecessors, existing targets, writes after sealing, and duplicate successors.
- [ ] Resetting command namespaces cannot allow old commands or awards to create rights again.
- [ ] Incompatible migration verifies offline; crashes preserve source sealing and successor uniqueness.
- [ ] CLI examples demonstrate one successful upgrade and one explicitly unsupported upgrade.

Depends on [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7), [Myelin#10](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/10), [Myelin#13](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/13); related: [Myelin#11](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/11), [Myelin#12](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/12). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[Successor validation](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L1231), [atomic successor test](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-store-rocksdb/tests/store.rs#L582), [reverse-lineage recovery](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L830).

issues.title: [P1] Define cross-host writer fencing and session migration recovery
issues.body:
## Why local CAS is insufficient

A head CAS in one RocksDB prevents two local writers from successfully finalizing the same height. After restoring another disk from backup or moving a session to another host, two databases can each pass their own CAS. Expiration of a routing lease does not revoke the old host's write or signing capability.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant O as Old worker
  participant A as Authoritative owner or quorum
  participant N as New worker
  O->>A: Stop admission and submit final drain head
  A->>A: Persist a higher fencing epoch
  A-->>N: New epoch and exact recovery anchor
  N->>N: Audit recovery and verify epoch before enabling writes
  O->>A: Write or signing request with old epoch
  A-->>O: Reject
```

## Design and implementation

- Define the authoritative source and durable state for ownership epochs/fencing tokens, including its failure and trust assumptions.
- Enforce fencing at authoritative storage, finality signer/committee, and external economic-effect boundaries. Gateway headers alone are insufficient.
- Distinguish moving the same session across processes/hosts from creating a successor after changing rules/consensus; the latter follows [Myelin#14](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/14).
- Do not declare automatic takeover safe if the old writer cannot be invalidated. Stop writes, or require closure and a verifiable new configuration.
- Specify the order of draining, stopping new commands, reconciling in-flight/unknown work, copying backups, auditing recovery, and enabling the new writer.
- Prevent cloned stores from independently signing with the same session authority key. Restores must validate the current epoch rather than trust a stale snapshot lease.
- Recover reservations through [Myelin#12](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/12) and reconcile remote claim terminal states.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With two independent RocksDB copies active, the old worker cannot produce progress or external rights accepted as canonical.
- [ ] Define outcomes for partitions, clock drift, lease expiry, takeover crashes, and stale-backup restores.
- [ ] Existing single-database CAS tests continue to pass.
- [ ] Unsafe takeover remains visibly blocked/pending rather than silently creating a new session and losing history.
- [ ] Publish a migration runbook and drill evidence without turning an ordinary Registry into a consensus component.

Prerequisite: [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7). Related: [Myelin#17](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/17), [Myelin#20](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/20), [UTXOPlay#4](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/4). issues.title: [P1] Complete archival, recovery budgets, and dependency retention for long-lived sessions
issues.body:
## Current behavior

RocksDB retains an archival snapshot every 256 blocks by default and atomically updates the latest complete checkpoint on every commit. Recovery audits the full block/proof history in pages; range replay can start from an earlier checkpoint. These are useful foundations, but bounded steps do not establish bounded lifetime disk usage, recovery time, or export memory.

Cross-session replay in B may also require A's old handoff, source block, authority, and program. B's latest snapshot alone cannot explain those dependencies.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  H["Hot storage: latest head and checkpoint"] --> A["Content-addressed archive"]
  B["Historical blocks, inputs, and proofs"] --> A
  D["Handoff and successor dependencies"] --> A
  P["Historical profiles and replayers"] --> A
  A --> V["Verified manifest and restore drill"]
  V --> R["Budgeted replay and cold recovery"]
```

## Deliverables

- Define retention for historical blocks, archival checkpoints, commands/nullifiers, handoff terminal states, outbox/evidence, and historical artifacts.
- Gate garbage collection on outstanding transfers, verifiable dependencies, and dispute/recovery requirements. Expiring short-lived logs must not make reward nullifiers usable again.
- Replace whole-chain export paths progressively with paginated/streamed bundles. Bound dependency depth, expanded bytes, replayed blocks, and wall time.
- Provide cancellation and progress reporting. Budget exhaustion returns a resumable checkpoint/cursor, not a "verified" result.
- State checkpoint trust: full genesis verification, trusted-anchor-plus-suffix replay, and full-range reexecution provide different assurance.
- Define consistent online backup/restore manifests; authority-key copying follows [Myelin#15](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/15).
- Build a cross-session dependency DAG, rejecting cycles and unbounded references. Copyable evidence and scarce claims need different collection rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Measure disk/RSS/recovery time for long histories, many active sessions, and dependencies across multiple epochs.
- [ ] Missing required data fails explicitly without silently skipping verification or downgrading to success.
- [ ] Restore archived history on a clean machine and replay old versions without the original service.
- [ ] Define measurement methods and deployment targets for RPO/RTO; do not infer fixed performance from source.
- [ ] Rebuilding indexes cannot change authoritative heads, rewards, or balances.

Depends on [Myelin#13](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/13) and [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7); related: [Myelin#20](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/20), [UTXOPlay#2](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/2). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[Storage policy and checkpoints](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-store-rocksdb/src/lib.rs#L37), [recovery audit](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L830), [range replay](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/replay.rs).

issues.title: [P1] Build reusable game adapters and determinism, time, and randomness integration contracts
issues.body:
## Scenario

Chess, Skyward, Block Party, and other games repeat executor, authority-verifier, snapshot, export/replay, and HTTP integration code while retaining different rules and performance needs. Myelin should provide thin reusable adapters and conformance tooling, with rules remaining in game repositories.

Support three explicit profile classes: command-driven turn-based games, deterministic tick tapes, and asynchronous economy/reward events. Turning every event into a CellTx must not be the only integration model.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  C["Browser inputs or commands"] --> H["Game-owned real-time loop"]
  H --> D["Replayable deterministic core"]
  D --> A["Thin Myelin application adapter"]
  A --> J["Journal, session, and commit"]
  J --> R["Receipt, snapshot, and export"]
  R --> V["Independent conformance verifier"]
```

## Deliverables

- Provide small adapters/templates for profile construction, finality adaptation, recovery, versioned export, and state queries. Keep game engines outside Myelin core.
- Unify command/receipt/status/error contracts for construction heads, durable IDs, reconnect, and Unknown. Clarify native-session API versus Web SDK responsibilities.
- Record result-affecting actor/seat admission, join/leave, timeouts, and AI takeover in replayable policy/events. Gateway headers do not prove personal player signatures on each action.
- Separate wall time, simulation ticks, frame cursor, and commit time. Batch boundaries must not change physics or scores.
- Pin RNG algorithm, seed/counter, and policy digest. A deterministic seed does not establish fair or manipulation-resistant randomness; economic random rewards need a separate entropy protocol.
- Define native/WASM numeric behavior, using fixed point or another explicit policy. Where floating point is used, differential tests must establish the claimed consistency; tolerance-based results cannot be presented as identical roots.
- Separate prediction/animation from committed gameplay. Handle mobile visibility/rotation, disconnection, and AI takeover according to the profile without changing old rules.
- Define hidden-information, private-input, and public-replay boundaries so evidence does not expose information affecting ongoing matches.
- Report CKB-VM cycles separately from host CPU/RSS. Reusing the SDK does not give historical host-replay profiles a court claim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A single-player save, a two-player turn-based game, and a fixed-tick multiplayer example pass the same integration checks.
- [ ] Identical inputs produce identical roots/results across native/browser, batching changes, and restart recovery.
- [ ] Duplicate, stale, and unauthorized commands, reconnects, and explicit timeout events have tested outcomes.
- [ ] Two downstream games adopt shared contracts while remaining independently runnable and releasable.
- [ ] Publish a capability manifest that rejects unsupported handoff or settlement operations.

Depends on [Myelin#12](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/12), [Myelin#9](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/9), [Myelin#13](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/13); downstream adoption: [UTXOPlay#4](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/4). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[TransitionExecutor](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L296), [ApplicationProfile](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/application.rs), [safety contracts](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/docs/architecture/session-safety.md).

issues.title: [P1] Measure latency, recovery, and session isolation with real game workloads
issues.body:
## Why measurements come next

The 756 passing tests establish covered behavior. They do not establish that 100ms batching suits every game or that sessions sharing a worker cannot delay each other. The external Teeworlds acceptance workload was explicitly skipped in the 0.31 release.

Use workload measurements to choose producer triggers, batch sizes, and capacity rather than infer TPS from architecture diagrams.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  W["Fixed inputs and workload seeds"] --> P["Producer strategy matrix"]
  P --> E["Host replay or real CellTx VM"]
  E --> S["Synchronous WAL commit"]
  S --> R["Client durable receipt"]
  S --> X["Archive and recovery drill"]
  R --> M["p50, p95, p99, and failure distributions"]
  X --> M
```

## Measurement scope

- Cover turn-based commands, single-player saves, fixed-tick multiplayer, and match-to-inventory rewards.
- Measure multiple sessions in one process and independent services separately. One overloaded/failing session must not monopolize queues, CPU, or global locks indefinitely.
- Separate input-to-simulation, input-to-durable-commit, proof collection, evidence publication, and cold replay latency.
- Compare Instant/Interval/Open/manual production, including window waiting and throughput/latency tradeoffs. Do not impose one 100ms/1024-event configuration everywhere.
- Measure executor cloning/snapshots, WAL, block/receipt/dependency-index growth, recovery scans, and export RSS.
- Inject lost ACKs, unknown producer outcomes, slow/offline evidence providers, disk quotas, worker restarts, and platform-index outages.
- Report zero-VM-cycle host execution separately from strict CKB-VM workloads. Retain machine/core counts, build versions, commits, input seeds, and raw results.
- Set deployment SLOs/capacity budgets after measurement; do not invent targets from source inspection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A newcomer can reproduce three workload scales and their raw reports with documented commands.
- [ ] Recommend trigger/resource settings for each game mode, with actual measurements.
- [ ] Fault checks verify heads, commands, rewards, and handoff conservation, not just process availability.
- [ ] Complete a long-history cold recovery drill and a cross-worker fencing drill.
- [ ] Report Teeworlds pass/skip/fail explicitly; missing external checkouts must not count as passing.

Related: [Myelin#19](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/19), [Myelin#18](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/18), [Myelin#9](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/9), [Myelin#15](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/15), [Myelin#21](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/21). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

issues.title: [P1] Split the production gate into portable, traceable CI acceptance lanes
issues.body:
## Current state

The production gate covers the workspace, pinned CellScript, parent CKB devnet, and optional external games. It still assumes developer-machine paths and external dependencies; the baseline tree has no .github/workflows. Historical concurrency documentation also contains stale statements about the absence of async runtimes and source-file sizes.

Contributors need to see which checks run independently, which require external assets, and exactly what a release executed.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P["PR or commit"] --> F["Formatting, compilation, and unit tests"]
  F --> C["Pinned compiler and compatibility vectors"]
  C --> D["Controlled CKB devnet acceptance"]
  D --> G["Explicit game integration lane"]
  F --> R["Report bound to commit and executed scope"]
  C --> R
  D --> R
  G --> R
```

## Scope

- Document dependencies for Linux, macOS, and clean containers. Discover CKB/Teeworlds through configuration or standard relative paths rather than a particular user's home directory.
- Separate fast core, compiler reproduction, CKB devnet, and game integration lanes. Report pass/fail/skip for each check.
- Bind compiler/toolchain, Cargo.lock, fixture hashes, and reports. Caches cannot bypass content/version verification.
- Expose each lane's network, version, resource, and optional-dependency requirements. Keep production authority keys and funded accounts out of ordinary CI.
- Require the selected release profile's acceptance lanes to actually run. Optional skips may allow unrelated contributions but must not imply a complete release pass.
- Refresh canonical architecture and historical plans so implemented capabilities, remote-transfer gaps, host replay, and CKB court claims agree.
- Tie documentation to executed integration checks; a historical 756-test record is not automatic proof of a current pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean runner executes the core lane without private filesystem paths.
- [ ] Missing external CKB/games produce explicit skips, distinguishable from required release failures.
- [ ] Reports link exact commits, logs, and artifacts.
- [ ] Map fmt/check/clippy/test and key integrations to explicit lanes.
- [ ] Module, async-boundary, and file-size descriptions match current code.
